verdict.rationale: Hyperbrowser supports natural-language commands via page.ai() and page.extract(), letting users direct browser actions and extraction with plain-language instructions, and also exposes an MCP server so AI agents can invoke tools via natural-language-driven prompts. However, this is scoped to page-level agent actions rather than full product operation (session management, profiles, stealth, etc. still require API/SDK calls, not NL commands), and there's no independent hands-on verification of page.ai() reliability. missing for 10: evidence that broader product operations (not just page actions) can be driven by NL, independent/third-party confirmation of page.ai() working reliably, and more detail on NL command scope/limits.
